_description: The ONE provenance vocabulary. Both memory-confidence-validator.py and handoff-provenance-lint.py load this table at runtime, so adding a value is a data change in one place rather than a code change in two. Repo pattern: allowlists load from a table at runtime.
_scar: 2026-07-28: memory-confidence-validator.py hardcoded a six-value enum; three days later handoff-provenance-lint.py shipped a different vocabulary for the same idea. Nothing collided because their file scopes differed, so the drift was invisible. See PRD prd-deterministic-reading-2026-07-28 Part C.
_rank_note: Higher rank wins when a line carries more than one form. A rank is a claim about how much the marker PROVES, not how confident the writer feels; `confidence` is a separate, orthogonal number and is not ranked here.

claim_id.means: points at an evidence.jsonl row carrying the command AND its output. Nothing the enum expresses is stronger than a recorded measurement.

validated.means: checked against a source, though no command is attached to the line

observed.means: seen directly in a tool result or artifact

explicit_statement.means: a person said it in so many words

corrected.means: revised after being wrong; the revision itself is not re-measured

imported.means: carried in from another system or session; provenance is that system's problem

inferred.means: reasoned to, not measured. The honest floor, not a failure.
